rationale: The workflow is a Go CI pipeline with lint, ubuntu-test, and windows-test jobs. Every job checks out code, sets up Go, and runs Go commands (vet, build, test, benchmark, golangci-lint) that repeatedly fetch module dependencies, but no dependency cache is present. The repository has go.mod and go.sum, satisfying the P-LIT-GHA-CACHE preconditions (repeated dependency fetching is measurable; cache inputs include the lockfile and environment). The matching experiment (batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9) added actions/cache@v4 for ~/go/pkg/mod keyed on runner OS plus hashFiles('go.mod', 'go.sum') and reported maintained success with 6.06% elapsed savings. Applying the same minimal cache step after checkout/setup-go and before Go commands preserves all existing build/test coverage and required checks without adding network access, secrets, or privileged actions.
